<summary>Agent "Research code graphs for impact and test reach" finished</summary>
<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>Report is at `/tmp/claude-1001/research/graph-codegraph.md`; the probe script is `graph_probe.py` in the same folder.

- **Already built:** ddflow already has a stdlib import-graph test selector. It is `services/testreach.py` plus `services/testselect.py`, which also use name, conftest, GOVERNS, identifier and data-file rules. The 2-hop cap, hub cut-off and 100-file budget are config defaults. A recall replay test exists (`tests/test_testselect_recall.py`).
- **Cost today:** 1470 py files (628 source, 810 test), 8107 edges. Cold build is 5.4 s with `testreach.build` and 4.3 s in my probe, and it is rebuilt on every `select()` call. The graph pickles to 119 KB.
- **Blast radius:** unbounded reverse closure is useless. The median source module reaches 459 of 810 tests, and p90 reaches 747. `core/records.py` reaches 747 tests (92%) and 404 modules. `api/review.py` reaches 452 tests (56%) and 90 modules.
- **Replay of 10 merges:** closure got recall 1.00 but reached 576 tests on average (71%). The existing selector got recall 0.92 and reached 77 (9.5%), with misses at 0.50 and 0.67. This is only a lower-bound proxy: truth is the tests changed in the merge, and the graph is HEAD's with the git inputs (changed files, identifiers) stubbed in. I did not run `ddflow tests`.
- **Literature:** Meta's predictive test selection catches >99.9% of faulty changes at one third of the tests. I did not re-verify the others from memory: Ekstazi runs about 32% of RetestAll time, and Google TAP selects by build-graph reachability. testmon is coverage-based and so not stdlib. Aider's repo map ranks files by PageRank within a 1k-token budget. SCIP needs external indexers, so it is overkill here.
- **Risks:** 33 files use importlib or `__import__`, and registry-by-convention, subprocess CLI tests and data files are invisible to imports. Safety net: the always-run guards list (DX-ci-always-run-guards), widening to the full suite when a dynamic-import or registry file changes, and the full merge queue staying as is.
- **Recommendation:** go on a small upgrade, no-go on a new graph subsystem, SCIP or full closure. Persist the graph in `.ddflow/cache/importgraph.json`, keyed per file by git blob hash and by a tree-hash fast path, using `git ls-files -s`. That should cut the warm build from 5.4 s to well under a second (I did not measure it). Add `ddflow graph blast <path>`. Then tune the hop cap and dynamic-import widening against the recall replay on real CI failures. The report has the full design.</result>

<summary>Agent "Audit graphs and graph gaps inside ddflow" finished</summary>
<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>The audit is written to `/tmp/claude-1001/research/graph-internal.md`. It lists 21 graphs ddflow already has or implicitly computes, a value/cost table of 14 candidate features, and where the current approach is fine. I didn't profile `ddflow tests` end to end or the `brief` and `recall` index builds, so those are marked open in the file.

The five highest-value findings:

1. **The scheduling graph is not the bottleneck.** On 2735 items, `schedule.plan()` takes 0.12 s, `critical_path` 0.02 s, and `waves()` 0.63 s. A `ddflow next` call takes 2.6 s, of which 1.7 s is reading the 65 MB log and folding it. `ddflow status` takes 6.9 s, of which 4.7 s is git subprocesses over 118 worktrees (`leases.scan`). Incremental wave or ready maintenance would save about 0.1 s, so skip it. A resident folded state (B-perf-mcp-start, P-perf) is worth more than any graph cache.
2. **The Python import graph is the one expensive graph, and it has no cache.** `services/testreach.py:build` parses 1487 files in 5.6 s on every selection (`ddflow tests`, `testselect`, `testscope`). Caching per-file imports by sha is the cheapest real win, and it is also the base for selective CI (B16, B4067086b6b).
3. **There is no single definition of the effective dependency edges.** Readiness, `critical_path`, `progress._waits_on` and the restamp scripts each re-derive them. That produced bugs B27, B67, B79c2f6e17a, B13ed484062, Bbbcbfc4bbb and B43447abfc8. A lazy `ItemGraph` view on `State` with `inherited_needs`, `dependents()` and `depth` is a correctness fix more than a speed one.
4. **Wave tags are a derived graph attribute stored by hand in the event log.** `/tmp/claude-1001/restamp_api.py` emits one update per task, and its pure-depth number disagrees with the glob-aware `core.schedule.waves` that only `plancheck` uses. Making depth and wave first-class derived values (after finding 3) removes the stale tags and the log churn.
5. **No impact query exists, though many open tasks need one.** P-context-sync.impact, .prompt and .conflict, PD-baseline, CN-consumers and B-dec-monitor all need "what does this change affect". That means open leases, items, decisions and tests it reaches, and each would otherwise write its own. Build it once from findings 2 and 3 plus glob overlap.

Two smaller items:
- **Duplicate graph code:** `roadmap_graph.reduce_edges` duplicates `core.graph.transitive_reduction`, which no production code calls. `plancheck.reaches` also duplicates `closure`.
- **Missing accessors:** there is no `dependents(id)` (four ad hoc scans) and no shared glob-conflict relation (five loops).</result>

The close used a test-file mutation (`--mutation-file`), since the fix touches only tests.

chunk_findings.detail: The doc justifies retry safety with "The worktree is adoptable: `create` returns the existing tree if present (worktree.py:219-223), which is what makes a retry after a lost reply safe", and states "plan_id replay returns the same plan". But the plan it emits is not idempotent: s2 is `argv:["git","worktree","add","-b","ddflow/probe-w","$REPO/.ddflow/worktrees/probe-w","origin/main"]`. Given the exact failure the doc says it handles (agent runs s1/s2, the reply is lost, agent replays plan_id and re-runs the steps), the second `git worktree add -b` fails with exit 128 ("a branch named 'ddflow/probe-w' already exists" / "already registered"), which the envelope's `expect.exit_codes:[0]` maps to a hard step failure. Adoption is Python logic inside `Worktree.create` and does not exist on the agent's side, so the "safe retry" claim holds only for the thin client, never for the envelope. Fix: emit a `git rev-parse --verify` / `git worktree list` pre-step with an alternate branch on the add, and let the report accept "already present" as success.

chunk_findings.detail: The same bullet that forbids secrets in argv also mandates delivering the declared command verbatim: "the one declared gate command that is a shell line by definition (`Declared.line`): it is delivered as `["sh","-c",line]`". Input: a gates.toml with `[gate.deploy] command = "curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-…' https://…"` (or any line with an inline `--token`/`-p` credential — common in real gates.toml). That literal is emitted into step s1 and therefore into the agent's/LLM's context, exactly the leak path the operator asked about in question (4); the server cannot redact it because the agent must execute the exact line. The adjacent field is also inconsistent with the rule: `env_hints: {"PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1"}` carries values, not "only `env_names`". Fix: carry `env_names` only (empty `env_hints`), and make the planner refuse/mark `unavailable` any `Declared.line` matching a secret heuristic instead of shipping it.

chunk_findings.detail: The headline result is contradicted two paragraphs later. Today `run_command_gate` records `tree_sha:"<head12>+st:<manifest>"` computed locally, and `complete` compares that evidence against the landed tree; under the envelope the doc itself says "It cannot compute `source_tree`'s dirty-content manifest, so client-exec requires push-before-gate … a gate on an unpushed dirty tree is `agent-reported` at best." So a gate run that is server-derived and `complete`-checkable today (development runs on a dirty tree, the normal `st:<manifest>` case) becomes honor-system under this mode — a verifiability downgrade, not "no gate becomes unverifiable". This matters because the sentence is the answer to the task's falsifier; the go/no-go should state that dirty-tree gates require the thin client and are simply not expressible in the envelope, rather than claiming parity.

chunk_findings.detail: The example asserts "refusals are server-side and unchanged: contested lease, gate blockers, nothing-to-land check (needs the pushed head)" in the very reply that returns `needs_local:true` with `s1 = git push origin ddflow/probe-w`. The parenthetical is the giveaway: the nothing-to-land decision requires the pushed commit, which only exists after s1 runs, so it cannot have been evaluated before the plan is emitted. Input: an item whose branch contains no changes relative to main — the agent gets a plan, pushes the branch to origin, and only in the report round trip is the "lands nothing" refusal produced; if the plan expires before the report, origin now holds a branch for an item the server never accepted, which the doc's own "expired => brief leads with it" recovery does not cover. The doc should either do a provisional check on the agent-supplied `head` in the first call or move the push into a separate plan.

chunk_findings.detail: The envelope comment calls `plan_id` "server-minted, single use", while the rules say "plan_id replay returns the same plan; a report for a plan that already has a report returns the recorded outcome" and the failure shapes rely on resuming a half-done plan. For the specific scenario the doc cares about (agent re-calls `ddflow_gate_run {exec:"client"}` after losing the reply), the spec does not say whether that is a replay of the live plan, a second plan with a new `plan_id` that orphans the first (and hence a second "plan pl_N half-done" entry in `brief`), or a rejection because the earlier plan is still live. That is the exact state machine task 5/6 must implement, so it should be stated one way.

chunk_findings.detail: The note identifies a real ddflow defect ("`ddflow gate record … --command` … is accepted and logged as `gate.passed`", mis-classified as tool-produced by `services/report_gates.py:15`), but only records it as task 0 of a task table — there is no bug id, no `bug_found` reference, and no duplicate/already-corrected check anywhere in the change (the probe record even says "no code in the repo was changed" while the change adds this file). The decision requires that defects discovered about ddflow itself be filed and checked for duplicates/already-fixed; a task row in a research note is not a filed defect, so the requirement is not demonstrated for the one ddflow bug this change found.

chunk_findings.detail: The label is claimed to be reachable only for a pushed *clean* tree, but cleanliness is not something the server can derive: the doc itself says the server "cannot compute `source_tree`'s dirty-content manifest", and the only cleanliness evidence in the envelope is agent-authored — step `s3`'s `git status --porcelain` stdout and the `tree={head, dirty}` field the agent puts in `ddflow_plan_report`. Input: an agent whose worktree has uncommitted edits runs pytest, pushes the last commit (`d77a9316378d`), and reports `s3:{stdout:""}` / `dirty:false` (or simply edits/omits the step, which the doc's own §4 says it may do). The server checks sha-on-remote (true), `command_digest` (also just the value it handed out in the plan — the report carries `id/exit/elapsed_s/output_digest/tail`, no argv, so `command_digest_matches:true` never establishes which command ran), and the blob digest, then returns `outcome:"passed", trust:"server-verified", tree_sha:"d77a9316378d+clean"` for code that was never exercised as pushed. That is precisely the dirty-tree run the section declares "not expressible", so the load-bearing claim of §3 (only `head+clean` gates are verifiable in client-exec) is unenforced; the `server-verified` name asserts server-derived verification of the one property that is purely agent-asserted. The doc's "honest bound" only concedes a fabricated *blob* "for a clean tree", not a false cleanliness report.

chunk_findings.detail: The two-round probe fixes re-invocation from scratch, but not the failure §1 says it handles ("a retry after a lost reply"). The probe runs *before* the mutation, so once the round-2 plan has been executed, a lost reply leaves the agent holding nothing; per the rule "Calling the tool again while a plan is live returns the SAME plan", replaying returns the same round-2 step `["git","worktree","add","-b","ddflow/probe-w","$REPO/.ddflow/worktrees/probe-w","origin/main"]`, which now fails with `fatal: a branch named 'ddflow/probe-w' already exists` — the plan is not re-runnable. The only escape offered ("a report of 'already present' counts as success") applies to the *probe* report, which was already consumed in round 1. Worked example A also still emits the single-round `-b` plan inline, contradicting the two-round description two bullets above it, and §1 still uses `Worktree.create`'s adoption (worktree.py:219-223) as the justification for retry safety although the agent has no adoption logic.

chunk_findings.detail: The quoted `GIT_TRACE` sequence cannot be executed: `git branch ddflow/<id> main` creates the branch, and the immediately following `git worktree add -b ddflow/<id> <path>` refuses because the branch now exists (`fatal: a branch named … already exists`). So either the trace is misread or `create` runs a different sequence; in both cases the plan derived in Worked example A (`git worktree add -b …` only, no branch step) is not equivalent to what `ddflow claim` actually does, which undercuts the "claim has exactly one tree-bound step / generated from the same declared commands" premise the envelope rests on. Input: run the two quoted commands in a scratch repo in order — the second exits non-zero.

chunk_findings.detail: The contract defines the `needs_local` envelope as the reply of *any* class-B tool when `[serve].exec = "client"` or the caller’s locality capability is `none`, but Section 5 says `NO-GO: general client-exec for all class-B tools` and explicitly only allows claim, gate run, and merge-as-PR. Given a remote server with no tree and a call to `ddflow_setup` or `ddflow_doctor` (both listed class B), Section 2 requires emitting a plan while Section 5 forbids implementing that plan. The deliverable’s contract and verdict are mutually contradictory.

chunk_findings.detail: Class A "pure state" includes `rule_list`, `rule_search`, `rule_show`, and `workflow_state`, but the same section states that `rule_*` and `workflow_*` are files under `.ddflow/rules/`/gates.toml. On a no-filesystem server, `ddflow_rule_list` or `ddflow_workflow_state` would need to read those local files and fail. The "74 pure-state tools" count and the remote-capable boundary are therefore incorrect, and the derived two-thirds/one-third split is wrong.

chunk_findings.detail: The bullet says "No secret ever appears in `argv`", but then says the declared gate shell line is delivered as `["sh","-c",line]`, so a secret literal in `line` is in `argv` unless the heuristic catches it. The envelope ships that value into the LLM context, violating its own no-secret rule and Section 4's "Secrets in commands: none" row.

chunk_findings.detail: The claim "the clean tree is by construction (fresh `git worktree add --detach <sha>` in the plan)" is not server-verified: that construction step runs on the agent’s host and is itself only agent-reported. A fake agent can skip or alter that construction, run the gate on a different/dirty tree, and report the expected `git rev-parse HEAD` and blob. The server would then record `checked.sha_on_remote: true` and `agent-run, server-checked`, although the run never occurred on the clean sha, so the stated falsifier ("cannot be made verifiable enough") is not refuted.

chunk_findings.detail: The envelope still asserts "No secret ever appears in `argv`", but the only controls are an operator `client_exec = true` self-attestation and an advisory heuristic. Input: a gate line `python3 deploy.py --api-key 3f9a...not-matched-by-heuristic` with `client_exec = true`; the line is emitted as `["sh","-c",line]` with `declared_by`. The secret literal then appears in `argv` and in the LLM context, contradicting the same bullet and Section 4's "Secrets in commands: none". The fix added DEFAULT-DENY/opt-in, but it does not enforce the stated invariant.

chunk_findings.detail: The `ddflow_gate_run` response prescribes only `s1` (`pytest`) and `s2` (`git rev-parse HEAD`), both with `cwd:"$WORKTREE"`, but it does not include the step that creates the fresh detached checkout of the pushed sha. The comment says `$WORKTREE` was "made by an earlier plan step", yet no such checkout step appears in the only plan response shown. An agent receiving this plan has no prescribed clean checkout path and can run the gate in a dirty or unrelated tree, defeating the `head+clean` verification it claims.

data.title: docs/ddflow/research/mcp-client-exec.md §1, evidence bullet "claim has exactly one tree-bound step"

chunk_findings.detail: The label is claimed to be reachable only for a pushed *clean* tree, but cleanliness is not something the server can derive: the doc itself says the server "cannot compute `source_tree`'s dirty-content manifest", and the only cleanliness evidence in the envelope is agent-authored — step `s3`'s `git status --porcelain` stdout and the `tree={head, dirty}` field the agent puts in `ddflow_plan_report`. Input: an agent whose worktree has uncommitted edits runs pytest, pushes the last commit (`d77a9316378d`), and reports `s3:{stdout:""}` / `dirty:false` (or simply edits/omits the step, which the doc's own §4 says it may do). The server checks sha-on-remote (true), `command_digest` (also just the value it handed out in the plan — the report carries `id/exit/elapsed_s/output_digest/tail`, no argv, so `command_digest_matches:true` never establishes which command ran), and the blob digest, then returns `outcome:"passed", trust:"server-verified", tree_sha:"d77a9316378d+clean"` for code that was never exercised as pushed. That is precisely the dirty-tree run the section declares "not expressible", so the load-bearing claim of §3 (only `head+clean` gates are verifiable in client-exec) is unenforced; the `server-verified` name asserts server-derived verification of the one property that is purely agent-asserted. The doc's "honest bound" only concedes a fabricated *blob* "for a clean tree", not a false cleanliness report.
chunk_findings.location: docs/ddflow/research/mcp-client-exec.md §3, `server-verified` row and "A gate run on a dirty tree … is NOT in client-exec … dirty-tree gates are not expressible in the envelope"
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/mcp-client-exec.md §3, `server-verified` row and "A gate run on a dirty tree … is NOT in client-exec … dirty-tree gates are not expressible in the envelope"

chunk_findings.detail: The two-round probe fixes re-invocation from scratch, but not the failure §1 says it handles ("a retry after a lost reply"). The probe runs *before* the mutation, so once the round-2 plan has been executed, a lost reply leaves the agent holding nothing; per the rule "Calling the tool again while a plan is live returns the SAME plan", replaying returns the same round-2 step `["git","worktree","add","-b","ddflow/probe-w","$REPO/.ddflow/worktrees/probe-w","origin/main"]`, which now fails with `fatal: a branch named 'ddflow/probe-w' already exists` — the plan is not re-runnable. The only escape offered ("a report of 'already present' counts as success") applies to the *probe* report, which was already consumed in round 1. Worked example A also still emits the single-round `-b` plan inline, contradicting the two-round description two bullets above it, and §1 still uses `Worktree.create`'s adoption (worktree.py:219-223) as the justification for retry safety although the agent has no adoption logic.
chunk_findings.location: docs/ddflow/research/mcp-client-exec.md §2 "Replay semantics, one way" and Worked example A step `s2`
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/mcp-client-exec.md §2 "Replay semantics, one way" and Worked example A step `s2`

chunk_findings.detail: The quoted `GIT_TRACE` sequence cannot be executed: `git branch ddflow/<id> main` creates the branch, and the immediately following `git worktree add -b ddflow/<id> <path>` refuses because the branch now exists (`fatal: a branch named … already exists`). So either the trace is misread or `create` runs a different sequence; in both cases the plan derived in Worked example A (`git worktree add -b …` only, no branch step) is not equivalent to what `ddflow claim` actually does, which undercuts the "claim has exactly one tree-bound step / generated from the same declared commands" premise the envelope rests on. Input: run the two quoted commands in a scratch repo in order — the second exits non-zero.
